verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच।
              इन्द्रप्रस्थे वसन्तस्ते जघ्रुरन्यान्नराधिपान्। शासनाद्धृतराष्ट्रस्य राज्ञः शान्तनवस्य च॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : When at the command of the king, Dhritarashtra and the son of Shantanu, (Bhishma), the Pandavas had taken up their abode at Indraprastha, they brought under their sway many other kings and monarchs.

verses.sanskrit: आश्रित्य धर्मराजानं सर्वलोकोऽवसत्सुखम्। पुण्यलक्षणकर्माणं स्वदेहमिव देहिनः॥२॥
verses.english: As a soul lives happily depending on the body blessed with auspicious marks and pious deeds, so all the subjects lived most happily, depending on Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira).

verses.sanskrit: स समं धर्मकामार्थान्सिषेवे भरतर्षभ। त्रीनिवात्मसमान्बन्धून्नीतिमानिव मानयन्॥३॥
verses.english: O best of the Bharata race, he (Yudhishthira) served equally Dharma, Artha and Kama, as if each of them was a friend as dear to him as his own soul.
verses.bhavadeepa: पुण्यानि लक्षणानि ऊर्ध्वरेखादीनि गाम्भीर्यादीनि च कर्माणि आरम्भकाणि क्रियमाणानि च यस्य तम् ॥२॥

verses.sanskrit: तेषां समविभक्तानां क्षितौ देहवतामिव। बभौ धर्मार्थकामानां चतुर्थ इव पार्थिवः॥४॥
verses.english: It appeared as if the three pursuits, Dharma, Artha and Kama, became personified on earth; and with them the king shined as the fourth (pursuit).

verses.sanskrit: अध्येतारं परं वेदान्प्रयोक्तारं महाध्वरे। रक्षितारं शुभाँल्लोकान्लेभिरे तं जनाधिपम्॥५॥
verses.english: Having obtained him as their king, they obtained a monarch who was devoted to the study of the Vedas, who was a performer of great sacrifices and who was the protector of all good works.
verses.bhavadeepa: तेषामिति । यथा त्रयाणाममात्यानां चतुर्थो राजा यथा आराध्यत्वेन भाति यथा वा धर्मार्थकामानां त्रयाणां चतुर्थो मोक्षस्वरूप आत्मा उत्तराध्यत्वेन भाति तथैनं धर्मादयः स्वयमुपतिष्टन्तीत्यर्थः ॥४॥

verses.sanskrit: अधिष्ठानवती लक्ष्मीः परायणवती मतिः। वर्धमानोऽखिलो धर्मस्तेनासीत्पृथिवीक्षिताम्॥६॥
verses.english: (During his reign) Lakshmi became stationary and hearts became devoted to the Supreme Spirit. Virtue itself began to grow all over the world.
verses.bhavadeepa: परम् अध्येतारं परस्य ब्रह्मणोधिगन्तारम् । वेदान्वेदानाम् । ब्रह्मकर्मनीतिनिष्टमिति विशेषणत्रयार्थः ॥५॥

verses.sanskrit: भ्रातृभिः सहितौ राजा चतुर्भिरधिकं बभौ। प्रयुज्यमानैर्विततो वेदैरिव महाध्वरः॥७॥
verses.english: Surrounded by his four brothers the king looked as resplendent as a great sacrifice depending upon and assisted by the four Vedas.
verses.bhavadeepa: अधिष्ठानेति । चलापि लक्ष्मीर्दृढास्पदाऽभूत् । परायणं परा काष्ठा तद्वती तां प्राप्तेत्यर्थः ॥६॥

verses.sanskrit: तं तु धौम्यादयो विप्राः परिवार्योपतस्थिरे। बृहस्पतिसमा मुख्याः प्रजापतिमिवामराः॥८॥
verses.english: Many learned Brahmanas with Dhaumya at their head, each equal to Brihaspati, waited upon the king, as the celestial wait upon the Lord of creation.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मराजे ह्यतिप्रीत्या पूर्णचन्द्र इवामले। प्रजानां रेमिरे तुल्यं नेत्राणि हृदयानि च॥९॥
verses.english: On account of the excessive affection of the people, both their hearts and eyes equally took great delight in Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) who was like a full moon without a stain.

verses.sanskrit: न तु केवलदैवेन प्रजा भावेन रेमिरे। यद्बभूव मनःकान्तं कर्मणा स चकार तत्॥१०॥
verses.english: The people took delight in him, not only because he was their king, but because they bore for him a great affection. The king also did not was agreeable to them.
verses.bhavadeepa: तुल्यं युगपत् । तुल्यमित्यत्र द्युत्येति पाठे द्युत्या नेत्राणि प्रीत्या हृदयानि च रेमिरे इत्यन्वयः ॥९॥

verses.sanskrit: न ह्ययुक्तं न चासत्यं नासह्यं न च वाऽप्रियम्। भाषितं चारुभाषस्य जज्ञे पार्थस्य धीमतः॥११॥
verses.english: The sweet-speeched and greatly intelligent son of Pritha (Yudhishthira) never uttered any was improper, or untrue unbearable or disagreeable.
verses.bhavadeepa: दैवेन देवो राजा तत्कर्मणा पालनेन न केवलं रमिरे अपि तु भावेन भक्त्या । तत्र हेतुः । यदिति । मनः कान्तं मनोरमं प्रजानाम् ॥१०॥

verses.sanskrit: स हि सर्वस्य लोकस्य हितमात्मन एव च। चिकीर्षन्सुमहातेजा रेमे भरतसत्तम॥१२॥
verses.english: or That greatly powerful and best king of the Varata race happily passed his days in seeking the good of every body, as if every one was his own self.
verses.bhavadeepa: कर्मणा प्रियकरत्वमुक्त्वा वाङ्मनसाभ्यामपि तदाह द्वाभ्याम् । न हीति । असह्यं दुःखदम् । अहितभिति पाठेपि स एवार्थः । अप्रियं प्रीत्यनुत्पादकम् । भाषितं वचनम् । जज्ञे प्रादुर्बभूव  ॥११॥

verses.sanskrit: तथा तु मुदिताः सर्वे पाण्डवा विगतज्वराः। अवसन्पृथिवीपालाँस्तापयन्तः स्वतेजसा॥१३॥
verses.english: (His brothers) the Pandavas brought by their great powers many kings under their sway; they passed their days in happiness, having nothing to disturb their peace.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कतिपयाहस्य बीभत्सुः कृष्णमब्रवीत्। उष्णानि कृष्ण वर्तन्ते गच्छावो यमुनां प्रति॥१४॥
verses.english: After a few days, Vivatsu (Arjuna) thus spoke to Krishna, “O Krishna, the summer is come, let us go to the Yamuna.

verses.sanskrit: सुहृज्जनवृतौ तत्र विहृत्य मधुसूदन। सायाह्ने पुनरेष्यावो रोचतां ते जनार्दन॥१५॥
verses.english: O Janardana, O slayer of Madhu, if you like, let us sport their with out friends and then return in the evening.

verses.sanskrit:
वासुदेव उवाच।
              कुन्तीमातर्ममाप्येतद्रोचते यद्वयं जले। सुहृज्जनवृताः पार्थ विहरेम यथासुखम्॥१६॥
verses.english: Krishna said : O son of Kunti, this is also my wish. O Partha, let us sport with our friends in the waters( of the Yamuna).

verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच।
              आमन्त्र्य तौ धर्मराजमनुज्ञाप्य च भारत। जग्मतुः पार्थगोविन्दौ सुहृज्जनवृतौ ततः॥१७॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said: O descendant of Bharata, having consulted with each other and after receiving Yudhishthira's permission, Partha (Arjuna) and Govinda (Krishna) in company with their friends set out (for the Yamuna).

verses.sanskrit: विहारदेशं संप्राप्य नानाद्रुममनुत्तमम्। गृहैरुच्चावचैर्युक्तं पुरन्दरपुरोपमम्॥१८॥
verses.english: And arrived at a charming spot, fitted for the purpose of pleasure, overgrown with numerous tall trees and adorned with high mansions and looking like the city of Indra. O descendant of Bharata, in these houses were collected for the descendants of Vrishni and Pritha (Arjuna and Krishna) numerous wellflavoured and costly viands, drinks and other articles of enjoyments and floral wreathes and various perfumes. The party soon entered the inner apartments (of the house), adorned with many precious gems of pure brilliancy. Entering these apartments, every one of them began to sport at his pleasure.

verses.sanskrit: भक्ष्यैर्भोज्यैश्च पेयैश्च रसवद्बिर्महाधनैः। माल्यैश्च विविधैर्गन्धैस्तथा वार्ष्मेयपार्थयोः॥१९॥
विवेशान्तःपुरं तूर्णं रत्नैरुच्चावचैः शुभैः। यथोपजोषं सर्वश्च जनश्चिक्रीड भारत॥२०॥
स्त्रियश्च विपुलश्रोष्ण्यश्चारुपीनपयोधराः। मदस्खलितगामिन्यश्चिक्रीडुर्वामलोचनाः॥२१॥
verses.english: The women with beautiful full hips and rising breasts with handsome eyes and unsteady gait for drink began to sport.

verses.sanskrit: वने काश्चिज्जले काश्चित्काश्चिद्वेश्मसु चाङ्गनाः। यथादेशं यथाप्रीति चिक्रीडुः पार्थकृष्णयोः॥२२॥
verses.english: Some sported at their pleasure in the woods, some in the waters and some within the houses as directed and commanded by Krishna and Partha (Arjuna).

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपदी च सुभद्रा च वासांस्याभरणानि च। प्रायच्छतां महाराज स्त्रीणां ते स्म मदोत्कटे॥२३॥
verses.english: O king, Draupadi and Subhadra, exhilarated with wine, gave away costly robes and ornaments to the women that were sporting there.

verses.sanskrit: काश्चित्प्रहृष्टा ननृतुश्चुक्रुशुश्च तथा पराः। जहसुश्च परा नार्यः पपुश्चान्या वरासवम्॥२४॥
verses.english: Some amongst them danced in joy and some began to sing; some laughed and jested and some drank excellent wines.

verses.sanskrit: रुरुधुश्चापरास्तत्र प्रजघ्नुश्च परस्परम्। मन्त्रयामासुरन्याश्च रहस्यानि परस्परम्॥२५॥
verses.english: Some obstructed one another's progress, some fought with one another and some again talked with one another in private and some cut jokes at one another.

verses.sanskrit: वेणुवीणामृदङ्गानां मनोज्ञानां च सर्वशः। शब्देन पूर्यते हर्म्यं तद्वनं सुमहर्द्धिमत्॥२६॥
verses.english: Those woods, filled with the charming music of the flute, guitars and drums, became the scene of prosperity itself.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिंस्तदा वर्तमानो कुरुदाशार्हनन्दनौ। समीपं जग्मतुः कंचिदुद्देशं सुमनोहरम्॥२७॥
verses.english: When such was the state of things there, the descendants of Kuru and Dasharha (Krishna and Arjuna) went to a certain charming spot near by.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र गत्वा महात्मानौ कृष्णौ परपुरञ्जयौ। महार्हासनयो राजंस्ततस्तौ सन्निषीदतुः॥२८॥
verses.english: O king, after having gone there, the two illustrious Krishna, the two subjugators of the hostile cities, (Krishna and Arjuna) sat themselves down on two very costly seats.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र पूर्वव्यतीतानि विक्रान्तानीतराणि च। बहूनि कथयित्वा तौ रेमाते पार्थमाधवौ॥२९॥
verses.english: Partha and Madhava amused themselves there by talking over their past achievements and discoursing on heroism and various other topics.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रोपविष्टौ मुदितौ नाकपृष्ठेऽश्विनाविव। अभ्यागच्छत्तदा विप्रो वासुदेवधनञ्जयौ॥३०॥
verses.english: When Vasudeva and Dhananjaya were thus happily sitting together (in that charming spot), like the twin Ashvinis in heaven, a certain Brahmanas came to them.

verses.sanskrit: बृहच्छालप्रतीकाशः प्रतप्तकनकप्रभः। हरिपिङ्गोज्ज्वलश्मश्रुः प्रमाणायामतः समः॥३१॥
verses.english: He looked like an old Shala tree, his complexion was like that of heated gold, his beard with bright yellow tinged with green, the height and thickness of his body were in just proportion.

verses.sanskrit: तरुणादित्यसङ्काशश्चीरवासा जटाधरः। पद्मपत्राननः पिङ्गस्तेजसा प्रज्वलन्निव॥३२॥
verses.english: He had matted locks, he was attired in rags, he was as effulgent as the morning sun, his eyes were like lotus-leaves, his colour was tawny and he appeared to be blazing in splendour.

verses.sanskrit: उपसृष्टं तु तं कृष्णो भ्राजमानं द्विजोत्तमम्। अर्जुनोवासुदेवश्च तूर्णमुत्पत्य तस्थतुः॥३३॥
verses.english: Seeing that foremost of Brahmanas blazing with splendour coming towards them, Arjuna and Vasudeva hastily rose up and stood waiting (to receive command).
